requirements.original: Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.
requirements.canonical: A union alternative SHALL be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.original: Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.
requirements.canonical: In a reference to a union alternative, TypeIdOrExpression SHALL resolve to the name of a union type or to an expression of a union type (e.g. a variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template or function invocation).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.original: AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.
requirements.canonical: In a reference to a union alternative, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to the name of an alternative of the union type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.

requirements.original: AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.
requirements.canonical: If the referenced value or template is of the anytype, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to a known type name or to a known type name qualified with a module name.
requirements.condition: the value or template is of the anytype
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.

requirements.original: Alternatives of union type definitions shall not reference themselves.
requirements.canonical: A union alternative SHALL NOT reference the union type definition it belongs to.

readings: A union alternative SHALL NOT be of the enclosing union type itself.
The type of a union alternative SHALL NOT refer, directly or indirectly, to the enclosing union type.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether only direct self-reference (alternative of the enclosing union type itself, giving an infinite type) is forbidden or also indirect recursion through other types; the direct reading is chosen since recursive types via e.g. record of are allowed elsewhere.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- Alternatives of union type definitions shall not reference themselves.

requirements.original: If an alternative in a union type or a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that alternative imposed by the constraints of the alternative declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored).
requirements.canonical: If a union alternative of a union type or of a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the type of the reference IS the set of values allowed by the constraints of the alternative declaration only, and constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored.
requirements.condition: an alternative is referenced by the dot notation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- If an alternative in a union type or a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that alternative imposed by the constraints of the alternative declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored).

requirements.original: When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced alternative is not the chosen alternative, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.condition: the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.

requirements.original: When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced union field or union value is omitted or uninitialized, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.condition: the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.

requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of a union type on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative shall become the chosen one.
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative SHALL become the chosen alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- When referencing an alternative of a union type on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative shall become the chosen one.

requirements.original: This rule shall apply recursively if the reference contains alternatives of nested unions, choosing all the referenced alternatives.
requirements.canonical: When a reference on the left hand side of an assignment contains alternatives of nested union values, all referenced alternatives SHALL become the chosen alternatives recursively.
requirements.condition: the reference contains alternatives of nested unions
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- This rule shall apply recursively if the reference contains alternatives of nested unions, choosing all the referenced alternatives.

requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative as follows:
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field, or of an omitted field (including a field omitted at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy), is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative.
requirements.condition: the union value or field is uninitialized or omitted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- When referencing an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative as follows:

requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of union type, the alternative referenced in the dot notation becomes the chosen one.
requirements.canonical: When a value or value field of a union type is expanded, the union alternative referenced in the dot notation IS made the chosen alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- a) When expanding a value or value field of union type, the alternative referenced in the dot notation becomes the chosen one.

requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, record of, set, set of, and array values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.
requirements.canonical: When expanding a left hand side reference to a union alternative, the expansion of record, record of, set, set of and array values and intermediate fields SHALL follow the rules of item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and of clause 6.2.2.1, correspondingly.

readings: Record and set values follow clause 6.2.1.1 a), record of and set of values follow clause 6.2.2.1, array values follow clause 6.2.7 a).
All listed kinds of values follow the rules of all three referenced clauses.
ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. The mapping of types to referenced clauses ("correspondingly") is not explicit; clause 6.2.1.1 covers record (and by reference set) types, 6.2.2.1 record of/set of, and 6.2.7 arrays, which is the chosen reading.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- b) Expansion of record, record of, set, set of, and array values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced alternative.
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value of the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced union alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.1 -- c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced alternative.

requirements.original: Optional fields are not allowed for the union type, which means that the optional keyword shall not be used with union types.
requirements.canonical: The `optional` keyword SHALL NOT be used for a union alternative.

ambiguity.issue: "Optional fields" and "used with union types" refer to union alternatives.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.2 -- Optional fields are not allowed for the union type, which means that the optional keyword shall not be used with union types.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of types for union alternatives nested within the union definition, similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.3.
requirements.canonical: A union type definition MAY contain nested type definitions for the types of its union alternatives, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.3.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.3 -- TTCN-3 supports the definition of types for union alternatives nested within the union definition, similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.3.

requirements.original: Embedded Fields with the union definition are similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.4.
requirements.canonical: A union type definition MAY contain embedded fields, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.4.

readings: The rules for embedded fields of record types in clause 6.2.1.4 apply unchanged to union types.
Embedded fields in union types follow analogous but not identical (unspecified) rules.
ambiguity.issue: "similar to" does not state whether the rules of clause 6.2.1.4 apply unchanged; the reading that they apply unchanged is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.5.4 -- Embedded Fields with the union definition are similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.4.

requirements.original: The special type anytype is defined as a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: The anytype IS a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The special type anytype is defined as a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: The address type shall be included if it has been explicitly defined within that module.
requirements.canonical: If the address type is explicitly defined within a module, the anytype of that module SHALL include the address type as an alternative.
requirements.condition: the address type has been explicitly defined within the module

readings: The anytype of a module SHALL include the address type only if the address type is defined in that module.
The anytype of a module SHALL include the address type if it is defined in or imported into that module.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether an address type imported into the module (rather than defined in it) is included; the reading "defined in the module itself" is chosen as it is literal.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The address type shall be included if it has been explicitly defined within that module.

requirements.original: The fieldnames of the anytype shall be uniquely identified by the corresponding type names.
requirements.canonical: Each field name of the anytype SHALL be the name of the corresponding type, identifying the field uniquely.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The fieldnames of the anytype shall be uniquely identified by the corresponding type names.

requirements.original: NOTE 1: As a result of this requirement imported types with clashing names (either with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module) cannot be reached via the anytype of the importing module.
requirements.canonical: An imported type whose name clashes with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module CANNOT be reached via the anytype of the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- NOTE 1: As a result of this requirement imported types with clashing names (either with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module) cannot be reached via the anytype of the importing module.

requirements.original: The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.
requirements.canonical: The anytype IS defined locally for each module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.

requirements.original: The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT directly import the anytype of another module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.

requirements.original: However, a user defined type of the type anytype can be imported by another module.
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type of the type anytype MAY be imported by another module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- However, a user defined type of the type anytype can be imported by another module.

requirements.original: The effect of this is that all types of that module are imported.
requirements.canonical: Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype IS the means by which all types of the module where it is declared become accessible (as its alternatives) in the importing module.

readings: Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype makes all types of the exporting module reachable as alternatives of that user-defined type.
Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype makes all types of the exporting module visible as definitions in the importing module.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the types become visible as importable definitions in the importing module or are only reachable as alternatives of the imported user-defined type; the latter reading is chosen, consistent with NOTE 2.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- The effect of this is that all types of that module are imported.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: The user-defined type of anytype "contains" all types imported into the module where it is declared.
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type of the type anytype IS a type containing all types imported into the module where it is declared.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.6 -- NOTE 2: The user-defined type of anytype "contains" all types imported into the module where it is declared.

requirements.original: Arrays can be used in TTCN-3 as a shorthand notation to specify record of types.
requirements.canonical: An array IS a shorthand notation to specify a record of type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Arrays can be used in TTCN-3 as a shorthand notation to specify record of types.

requirements.original: They may be specified also at the point of a variable, formal parameter or function return value declaration.
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be specified at the point of a variable declaration, formal parameter declaration or function return value declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- They may be specified also at the point of a variable, formal parameter or function return value declaration.

requirements.original: Arrays may be declared as single or multi-dimensional.
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be declared as single-dimensional or multi-dimensional.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Arrays may be declared as single or multi-dimensional.

requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.
requirements.canonical: An array dimension SHALL be specified using a constant expression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.
requirements.canonical: A constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL evaluate to a positive integer value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Constants used in the constant expressions shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.
requirements.canonical: An array element IS accessed by means of the index notation ([]).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.
requirements.canonical: The index notation used to access an array element SHALL specify a valid index within the array's range.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

requirements.original: Individual elements of multi-dimensional arrays can be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a multi-dimensional array CAN be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Individual elements of multi-dimensional arrays can be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.

requirements.original: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.
requirements.canonical: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.

readings: An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length MAY be used as index, its length being equal to the number of indexed dimensions.
An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length not exceeding the number of dimensions MAY be used as index, yielding an array slice.
ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "restricted to a single size" is read as a fixed length restriction; it is not stated whether that size must equal the number of dimensions of the indexed array.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- An array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.

requirements.original: Accessing elements outside the array's range will cause a compile-time or test case error.
requirements.canonical: Accessing an element outside the array's range SHALL cause a compile-time error or a test case error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Accessing elements outside the array's range will cause a compile-time or test case error.

requirements.original: Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).
requirements.canonical: An array dimension MAY be specified using a range.

examples.text:
type integer MyArrayType2[2 .. 5]; // A type with 4 integer elements, indices starting with 2
  type record length (4) of integer MyRecordOfType2; // The corresponding record of
  var integer v_myArray3[1 .. 5]; // Instantiates an integer array of 5 elements
                     // with the index 1 to 5
  v_myArray3[1] := 10; // Lowest index
  v_myArray3[5] := 50; // Highest index
  var integer v_myArray4[1 .. 5][2 .. 3 ]; // Instantiates a two-dimensional integer array of
                            // 5 × 2 elements with indexes from (1,2) to (5,3)

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).

requirements.original: Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).
requirements.canonical: A range specifying an array dimension SHALL have inclusive boundaries only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).

requirements.original: In such cases, the lower and upper values of the range syntax define the lower and upper index values.
requirements.canonical: The lower and upper value of a range specifying an array dimension IS the lower and upper index value of that dimension, respectively.

examples.text:
type integer MyArrayType2[2 .. 5]; // A type with 4 integer elements, indices starting with 2
  type record length (4) of integer MyRecordOfType2; // The corresponding record of
  var integer v_myArray3[1 .. 5]; // Instantiates an integer array of 5 elements
                     // with the index 1 to 5
  v_myArray3[1] := 10; // Lowest index
  v_myArray3[5] := 50; // Highest index
  var integer v_myArray4[1 .. 5][2 .. 3 ]; // Instantiates a two-dimensional integer array of
                            // 5 × 2 elements with indexes from (1,2) to (5,3)

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- In such cases, the lower and upper values of the range syntax define the lower and upper index values.

requirements.original: The upper value shall not be lesser than the corresponding lower value.
requirements.canonical: The upper value of a range specifying an array dimension SHALL NOT be less than the corresponding lower value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- The upper value shall not be lesser than the corresponding lower value.

requirements.original: Such an array is corresponding to a record of with a fixed length restriction computed as the difference between upper and lower index bound plus 1 and indexing starting from the lower bound of the array definition.
requirements.canonical: An array whose dimension is specified by a range IS equivalent to a record of type with a fixed length restriction of (upper bound - lower bound + 1), with indexing starting from the lower bound.
requirements.condition: the array dimension is specified using a range

examples.text:
type integer MyArrayType2[2 .. 5]; // A type with 4 integer elements, indices starting with 2
  type record length (4) of integer MyRecordOfType2; // The corresponding record of
  var integer v_myArray3[1 .. 5]; // Instantiates an integer array of 5 elements
                     // with the index 1 to 5
  v_myArray3[1] := 10; // Lowest index
  v_myArray3[5] := 50; // Highest index
  var integer v_myArray4[1 .. 5][2 .. 3 ]; // Instantiates a two-dimensional integer array of
                            // 5 × 2 elements with indexes from (1,2) to (5,3)

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Such an array is corresponding to a record of with a fixed length restriction computed as the difference between upper and lower index bound plus 1 and indexing starting from the lower bound of the array definition.

requirements.original: NOTE: It is not possible to define an array type with a variable amount of elements.
requirements.canonical: An array type with a variable number of elements CANNOT be defined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- NOTE: It is not possible to define an array type with a variable amount of elements.

requirements.original: Neither is it possible to define an unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index.
requirements.canonical: An unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index CANNOT be defined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Neither is it possible to define an unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index.

requirements.original: The values of array elements shall be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.
requirements.canonical: The value of an array element SHALL be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- The values of array elements shall be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.

requirements.original: Values may be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation or more than one or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.
requirements.canonical: Values of array elements MAY be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation, or several or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.

ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "index assignment notation" is not a defined term; the assignment notation with indexes (clause 6.2.2.4) is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Values may be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation or more than one or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.

requirements.original: For using the value list or assignment notation for arrays, the rules described in clause 6.2.2.4 are valid for arrays as well.
requirements.canonical: The value list notation and assignment notation for an array IS subject to the rules of clause 6.2.2.4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- For using the value list or assignment notation for arrays, the rules described in clause 6.2.2.4 are valid for arrays as well.

requirements.original: Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.
requirements.canonical: The index notation MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.

requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero or the lower bound if an index range has been given.
requirements.canonical: The index of the first element of an array SHALL be zero, or the lower bound of the index range if an index range has been given.

examples.text:
type integer MyArrayType2[2 .. 5]; // A type with 4 integer elements, indices starting with 2
  type record length (4) of integer MyRecordOfType2; // The corresponding record of
  var integer v_myArray3[1 .. 5]; // Instantiates an integer array of 5 elements
                     // with the index 1 to 5
  v_myArray3[1] := 10; // Lowest index
  v_myArray3[5] := 50; // Highest index
  var integer v_myArray4[1 .. 5][2 .. 3 ]; // Instantiates a two-dimensional integer array of
                            // 5 × 2 elements with indexes from (1,2) to (5,3)

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- The index of the first element shall be zero or the lower bound if an index range has been given.

requirements.original: The index shall not exceed the limitations given by either the length or the upper bound of the index.
requirements.canonical: An array index SHALL NOT exceed the limitations given by the length or by the upper bound of the index range.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- The index shall not exceed the limitations given by either the length or the upper bound of the index.

requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.
requirements.canonical: If the value of the array element indicated by the index on the right hand side of an assignment is undefined, an error SHALL be caused.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.

requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.
requirements.canonical: If the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, an error SHALL be caused.
requirements.condition: the array value is uninitialized or omitted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.

requirements.original: Sending an array value with undefined elements shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Sending an array value with undefined elements SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Sending an array value with undefined elements shall cause an error.

requirements.original: All elements in an array value that are not set explicitly are undefined.
requirements.canonical: An array element that is not set explicitly IS undefined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- All elements in an array value that are not set explicitly are undefined.

requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized array value or field or omitted field on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values specified in clause 6.2.2.4 apply.
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized array value or field or of an omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values of clause 6.2.2.4 SHALL apply.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- When referencing an element of an uninitialized array value or field or omitted field on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values specified in clause 6.2.2.4 apply.

requirements.original: For assigning values to multi-dimensional arrays, each dimension that is assigned shall resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.
requirements.canonical: When assigning a value to a multi-dimensional array, each dimension that is assigned SHALL resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- For assigning values to multi-dimensional arrays, each dimension that is assigned shall resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.

requirements.original: When specifying values for multi-dimensional arrays, the leftmost dimension corresponds to the outermost structure of the value, and the rightmost dimension to the innermost structure.
requirements.canonical: In a value for a multi-dimensional array, the leftmost dimension IS the outermost structure of the value and the rightmost dimension IS the innermost structure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- When specifying values for multi-dimensional arrays, the leftmost dimension corresponds to the outermost structure of the value, and the rightmost dimension to the innermost structure.

requirements.original: The use of array slices of multi-dimensional arrays, i.e. when the number of indexes of the array value is less than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition, is allowed.
requirements.canonical: An array slice of a multi-dimensional array MAY be used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- The use of array slices of multi-dimensional arrays, i.e. when the number of indexes of the array value is less than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition, is allowed.

requirements.original: Indexes of array slices shall correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right (i.e. the first index of the slice corresponds to the first dimension of the definition).
requirements.canonical: The indexes of an array slice SHALL correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Indexes of array slices shall correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right (i.e. the first index of the slice corresponds to the first dimension of the definition).

requirements.original: Slice indexes shall conform to the related array definition dimensions.
requirements.canonical: The indexes of an array slice SHALL conform to the related dimensions of the array definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.7 -- Slice indexes shall conform to the related array definition dimensions.
